label: Figure 14.4: The relationship between investment and the interest rate
alt: A downward-sloping investment curve I. When the interest rate falls from 7% to 4%, investment rises from I1 to I2.
caption: Investment falls as the interest rate rises. A fall in the interest rate from 7% to 4% is a movement down along the curve, from I1 to I2: borrowing is cheaper and saving less attractive, so the level of investment increases. A rise in the rate would move the economy the other way, to lower investment.
